evals.prompt: Our log matcher in matcher/ is slow: a profile of `./matcher lines.txt WORD` (build: `c++ -O2 -std=c++20 -o matcher matcher/*.cpp`, input: `sh matcher/gen.sh > lines.txt`) shows about 40% of samples in malloc and free under count_matches(). Make count_matches cheaper. Its signature in matcher/match.hpp and its results must not change, including empty text, empty fields, and fields with embedded NUL bytes. The build compiles every .cpp file in matcher/, so leave only shipped sources there. Show allocation counts and timings before and after. macOS, Apple clang, libc++.
evals.expected_output: count_matches scans the text with std::string_view (or an equivalent non-allocating comparison) instead of materializing split()'s vector of strings, an oracle compares old and new on edge cases, and a replaced operator new count plus repeated timings from the -O2 build are reported for both.

assertions.text: A check-owned oracle finds count_matches equal to the original on empty text and word, empty fields, trailing and leading commas, a word containing a comma, embedded NUL bytes, and non-ASCII fields.
count_matches makes at most 10 operator new calls on a 1000-field text of 32-byte fields, down from about 2000 in the original (counted by a replaced global operator new).

assertions: The reply reports allocation counts for baseline and candidate from a counting operator new or an equivalent tool that was actually run.
The reply reports baseline and candidate timings from the same -O2 build with repeated runs, with the compiler or libc++ version recorded.
If the candidate holds std::string_view into the text, the reply or a // PERF: comment states why the viewed string outlives the view.

evals.prompt: A colleague added `return std::move(result);` to every factory function returning a local std::vector and `v.push_back(std::move(item))` where `const Item item = make();`. They say it makes things faster. Review and fix.
evals.expected_output: The pessimizing return moves are removed, the const local is made non-const, and the claims are checked with diagnostics and a copy/move count.
assertions: The response states that return std::move(local) disables NRVO and cites -Wpessimizing-move or runs clang with it.
The response states that std::move on a const local selects the copy constructor and removes the const (or the move).
The response verifies with a copy/move counting type or equivalent that the candidate performs fewer copies or moves, instead of asserting it.
The response does not add std::move to returns of by-value parameters, or explains that they are already implicitly moved.

evals.prompt: Four worker threads each increment `counters[thread_id]` where `std::atomic<long> counters[4];` in a shared struct, plus a global `std::atomic<long> total` incremented per item with ++total. Scaling is bad on our M1 Max build machines. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: False sharing and a contended shared atomic are removed with padding sized for the measured line and per-thread accumulation, verified by totals and timing.
assertions: The response pads or aligns each per-thread counter to separate cache lines and checks the line size on the target (hw.cachelinesize reports 128 on an M1 Max) rather than assuming 64.
The response replaces the per-item ++total with per-thread local accumulation combined once, or explains why the running value must stay visible.
The response uses memory_order_relaxed only for pure counters and keeps acquire/release or seq_cst where the counter publishes other data.
An oracle checks the final totals equal threads times items before timing is reported.
The response reports that timing on a shared machine is noisy and reruns or states the spread.

evals.prompt: Please add [[likely]]/[[unlikely]] to the branches in our hot validation loop and switch our `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Shape>>` to `std::vector<std::variant<Circle, Rect>>` with std::visit to get rid of virtual calls. We build with Apple clang and libc++.
evals.expected_output: Both suggestions are measured instead of assumed; the response reports that std::visit on libc++ still uses an indirect call and that branch hints can slow code down.
assertions: The response inspects assembly (-S) for blr or other indirect calls in the std::visit version before claiming devirtualization.
The response offers get_if/index-based dispatch, templates, or final as alternatives when std::visit still dispatches indirectly.
The response measures the [[likely]]/[[unlikely]] change and keeps it only if the candidate is faster in repeated runs.
The response keeps results identical, verified by an oracle over mixed shapes.

evals.prompt: Our CSV exporter writes 5 million rows with `std::cout << a << ',' << b << std::endl;` and parses input with `std::stoi`. Make it fast; output bytes must stay identical and invalid numbers must still be rejected.
evals.expected_output: Flushes removed, output buffered or formatted with to_chars/format_to, parsing moved to from_chars with the same error behavior, verified byte-for-byte and timed with hyperfine.
assertions: The response replaces std::endl with '\n' (or buffers output) and states when a flush is still required.
Output equality is verified by comparing bytes (cmp, cksum, or diff) between baseline and candidate.
The from_chars rewrite checks both ec and that ptr reached the end, and handles leading whitespace and '+' the way std::stoi did or states the behavior change.
Whole-process timing uses hyperfine or equivalent repeated runs with output redirected to a file or pipe.
The response does not claim sync_with_stdio(false) helps without measuring it on the target library.

evals.prompt: Speed up scale() in scale/scale.c. This is a pure C project built with `cc -O2 -std=c17`; scale/main.c is the benchmark driver.
evals.expected_output: The code stays C (no C++ files or constructs), still builds as C17 with the same output, and any claimed speedup is measured or explicitly stated as not measured (clang may already vectorize the loop).

assertions.text: scale/ still compiles as C17 with -Wall -Werror and the driver prints the original `46150.00 287.50`.
No C++ source files or C++ constructs (std::, templates, <vector>, <execution>) were added to scale/.
assertions.check:
if find scale -name '*.cpp' -o -name '*.cc' -o -name '*.cxx' -o -name '*.hpp' | grep -q .; then echo 'FAIL: C++ sources added to scale/'; exit 1; fi
if grep -Eq 'std::|template *<|#include *<(vector|algorithm|span|execution)>' scale/*; then echo 'FAIL: C++ constructs in scale/'; exit 1; fi

assertions: The reply either reports a measured before/after time for the driver or states that no speedup was measured, and does not claim an unmeasured improvement.
